text:
**Short answer:** about 200-400 W of solar. A 200 W panel refills a 1,000 Wh station in roughly 1.5 days of decent sun, and about 300-350 W does it in one good day.

**The formula** (panel watts × peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75 real-world efficiency = Wh per day):

- A 200 W panel at 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency gives about 630 Wh/day, so a 1,000 Wh station takes about 1.5 days ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- A 400 W panel gives about 1,260 Wh/day, so it refills in under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- Rule of thumb: battery Wh ÷ 5 gives the panel watts that recharge it in about a day and a half ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Panel watts for a full recharge in one day** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

Winter in the northern US, with about 2 sun hours, needs roughly 700 W or more for a one-day recharge ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Before you buy:**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-400 W or more, and panels beyond the cap add nothing on a clear day. Check your model's spec sheet.
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window. Exceeding it can damage the unit, and wiring panels in series adds voltage.
- **Connectors:** Confirm the adapter (MC4 to XT60, DC barrel, etc.) fits.
- **Running loads:** If you draw power while charging, subtract that from the solar input. Recharging will be slower.

If you tell me your station model and where you'll use it, I can narrow this down and suggest compatible panels.
